subject: Inter-region handoff increased RTT — PulsePoint production p95/p99 spike
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@pulsepoint.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng-ops@pulsepoint.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spike — p95 up ~300ms since 08:05 PDT

Hi Mina,

We're seeing a sharp jump in p95 and p99 latency across our production calls to Redwood's hosted API beginning ~08:05 PDT this morning. The p95 has increased by ~300ms and p99 by ~900ms. Error rate is low but throughput is impacted as clients retry.

Quick notes from our side:
- Affected region: US (us-east-1 primarily)
- Example traces: https://app.datadog.com/rum/trace/abc123 (sample)
- We attached a brief trace PDF and a snapshot of our client metrics.

Can your ops team confirm if anything changed on Redwood's side (routing, peering, config) around that time? This is causing noticeable degradation for our customers.

Thanks,
Maria
Head of SRE — PulsePoint Health
Attachments: ddi-trace-brief.pdf, pulsepoint-p95-graphs.png
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@pulsepoint.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — p95 up ~300ms since 08:05 PDT

Hi Maria — thanks for the heads up and the traces. I'm escalating this to our SRE and networking leads (Sean and Rishi) and looping in Laura from Customer Success so we can coordinate incident comms.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Sean / Rishi: can you triage network egress/routing and check for any region-to-region handoff anomalies starting ~08:00–08:15 PDT?
- Sean: please share a short mitigation plan we can offer PulsePoint (pinning, immediate routing override, or temporary capacity shift).
- Rishi: confirm whether any managed peering / egress policy changed overnight or during the 07:00–09:00 PDT window.

Maria — we'll come back with an ETA for mitigation within 30 minutes. Sorry for the disruption.

— Mina
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mina Haddad | mina.haddad@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 08:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — p95 up ~300ms since 08:05 PDT

I've pulled traces and observed a pattern where client sessions for PulsePoint are being handed off to our eu-west-1 egress path for a subset of traffic, which adds an extra inter-region hop (us-east -> eu-west -> us-east) in some flows. That matches the RTT inflation.

Preliminary findings:
- At ~08:04 PDT a routing policy change was deployed to rollout a new traffic-splitting rule (internal flag: rollout/v2). The new rule included a hostname regex that accidentally matched part of pulsepoint client hostnames, causing ~12% of requests to pick eu-west egress.
- Traces show increased SYN/ACK and TLS handshake RTTs for the affected sessions; p99 tails correlate with the longer path.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Apply a temporary routing override to pin PulsePoint traffic to the us-east egress (we can push in ~10 minutes).
2) Enable model-variant local fallback (route to a compatible us-east variant) — lower risk but needs quick config update.
3) Roll back rollout/v2 entirely (fast, but broader impact if rollout had other fixes).

I'll prepare the override and a quick patch; Rishi, if you can confirm the route rule diff and whether we can target just PulsePoint CIDR ranges, we can do option 1 immediately.

Sean
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: edge-routing-diff.txt
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — p95 up ~300ms since 08:05 PDT

Confirmed — I inspected the routing rules and can reproduce the mis-match in the rollout/v2 policy. The regex intended to match internal-service.example.com accidentally treated pulsepoint.ai subdomains as a match due to an unanchored token. The change was deployed at 07:58 PDT to a small inhale group.

Actions taken so far:
- Reverted the rollout/v2 rule at 09:00 PDT (route rule reverted to prior state).
- Pushed an explicit egress override for PulsePoint CIDR ranges (10.14.32.0/22 and 10.14.36.0/22) at 09:12 PDT to force us-east egress for new sessions.
- Captured a route table snapshot (route-table-snapshot.json) and the diff (edge-routing-diff.txt) for the postmortem.

Notes: residual sessions that were already established with eu-west egress may persist until client TLS session timeouts/keepalives expire; that explains degradation lasting beyond the revert. Rolling rollback was quick; full return to nominal p95 expected within 2–3 hours as sessions drain.

Next steps:
- I'll coordinate with AWS Support to confirm NAT gateway peering state if we continue to see unexpected cross-region hairpins.
- We'll harden the regex tests and add a pre-deploy integration check to catch host-based mis-matches.

Rishi
Edge Networking Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@pulsepoint.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, aws-support@amazon.com
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — p95 up ~300ms since 08:05 PDT

Maria — short update and proposed remediation.

What happened (brief): a routing rollout included an unanchored hostname regex that matched a subset of PulsePoint traffic and caused those requests to be routed through our eu-west egress. That extra hop increased RTT and produced the p95/p99 inflation you observed.

What we did:
- Reverted the rollout at 09:00 PDT and pushed an explicit egress override for PulsePoint at 09:12 PDT.
- Collected traces and route table snapshots; we've attached the artifacts.
- Eng expects session drains to bring p95 back to baseline within 2–3 hours; we've been tracking steady improvement since ~11:00 PDT.

Customer-focused remediation:
- One-time credit equal to 10% of April 2029 billed usage for PulsePoint (we can adjust if you prefer a fixed credit).
- A short post-incident call with our Edge Networking lead and SRE to walk through root cause and recovery actions (30–45 minutes).
- Action items: tighter pre-deploy tests for hostname matching, integration test in canary for egress policies, and an emergency runbook to pin VIPs in cases of cross-region handoff.

Please find a draft action plan attached (MAP-Action-Plan.md). We can schedule the follow-up call today or tomorrow. I apologise for the impact — we'll own the follow-up and make sure this doesn't recur.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: MAP-Action-Plan.md, route-table-snapshot.json
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@pulsepoint.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng-ops@pulsepoint.ai, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — p95 up ~300ms since 08:05 PDT

Thanks Mina — appreciate the quick investigation and the clear action items. We can take the 10% credit and would like to schedule the follow-up call at 10:00 PDT tomorrow. Please include Rishi and Sean.

For now we're seeing p95 trending back toward baseline; we'll monitor and let you know if anything persists.

— Maria
Maria Gonzalez, Head of SRE — PulsePoint Health
